raw_response:
I'm a 48-year-old farmer in Quzhou County with 20 years under my belt. I've got 10.1 mu of decent flat land here, and my household has four people — my wife and I do most of the farm work, but my son works at a factory in town, so he's only around for the big rush at harvest. That means labor is tight, especially during that week between wheat coming off and maize going in.

For the winter wheat, I'm planting around October 12th, same timing as every year. The extension fellow last winter said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've been farming this plot long enough to know my soil can handle a bit more if I want decent yield. I'll put down about 35 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer before planting — that's the 15-15-15 type from the co-op. Then come March, when the wheat is at jointing, I'll spread about 25 kg of urea per mu. If the crop looks strong and green by heading stage, I might skip a second topdressing, but if it's yellowing I'll throw another 10 kg on. I'd rather waste a little money on extra fertilizer than lose yield — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps.

For irrigation, I'll water before winter if the soil is dry, then once at jointing, and again around grain filling. Three times total. The water meter costs me about 25 yuan each time per mu, so that's real money, but you can't skip it and expect good wheat around here. For pesticides, I'll spray herbicide after planting and keep an eye out for aphids — if they show up, I'll use insecticide.

The wheat should come off around June 10th. Then the real rush starts. My neighbor and I help each other — he has a small rotary tiller. We'll till the stubble right after harvest and get the maize in the ground by June 13th at the latest. That window is never more than five days, so we can't mess around. I buy hybrid maize seed fresh every year — usually something like Zhengdan 958, costs about 45 yuan per mu. You can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't work. I'll put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, about 30 kg per mu, then topdress with 20 kg of urea when the maize hits the big trumpet stage in July. For maize irrigation, I'll water once at trumpet stage and maybe again at tasseling if it's dry — usually twice is enough since summer rains normally help out.

I'm expecting about 450 kg per mu for wheat and around 500 kg per mu for maize if the weather doesn't do anything strange. Total input costs will run me about 5,200 yuan for the year — seed, fertilizer, water, and chemicals for both crops. My son sends some money home from his factory job, so I can afford the inputs without cutting corners, but I still watch every yuan. No point throwing money away.
